meta.title: Bugping — bug reports and feedback in Telegram & Discord
meta.description: A ≈15 KB feedback widget with screenshots and markup. Reports land in Telegram or Discord within seconds. Free to start.

hero.title: Catch bugs earlier — before your customers leave
hero.subtitle: Visitors report a problem in two clicks, with a screenshot they can mark up. You get it in Telegram or Discord within seconds — with the page, browser and console errors attached.

facts.label: Bugping in numbers
facts.freeLabel: to start on the Free plan
facts.worksOn: Works on any site where you can add a script:

features.title: Everything a good bug report needs
features.subtitle: Visitors don’t have to explain the problem in words: the widget collects the context for them.

shot.title: Screenshot & markup
shot.body: One click captures the page. Visitors box the problem, draw with a pen or hide private data — or attach their own image by pasting or dropping it.

chat.title: Instantly in your chat
chat.body: Every report arrives in Telegram or Discord within seconds, with the screenshot and all the details.

context.title: Full context
context.body: Page URL, browser, OS, screen size, language and recent console errors are attached automatically.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.body: All reports in one place: filter by type, mark them resolved or archive them, open screenshots full size.

light.title: Lightweight
light.body: ≈15 KB gzipped, loaded async when the browser is idle. The screenshot code loads only when it’s needed.

brand.title: Your brand
brand.body: Pick the colour, position, button text and language. On Pro, remove the badge and add your own CSS.

how.title: Up and running in three steps
how.subtitle: No SDK, no build step: one script tag.
how.step1Body: Sign in with GitHub or email and create a project for your site.
how.step2Body: Paste the snippet before '</body>' — your project’s key is on its Install page.
how.step3Body: Link Telegram or Discord in Integrations, and reports start arriving.

audience.title: Who it’s for
audience.subtitle: Anyone whose website should work — and who’d rather hear about it when it doesn’t.
audience.devBody: Bug reports with a screenshot and console errors instead of “it doesn’t work”. Call identify() to know which user sent it.
audience.shopBody: Customers tell you about a broken checkout or a wrong price before they leave for a competitor.
audience.studioBody: Clients leave comments right on the site, marked up on a screenshot. On Pro, one project per client site, as many as you need.

author.title: From the author
author.body1: Hi! I built Bugping because users rarely report bugs — they just leave. I wanted reporting to take two clicks and to land where developers already are: in the chat.
author.body2: No heavy scripts, no per-seat pricing, nothing to configure for a week — just a widget that does its job.
author.tryWidget: Missing something or found a bug? The button in the corner of this page is the real Bugping widget — tell me there, I read every report.

faq.title: Questions & answers
faq.subtitle: Didn’t find yours? Ask through the widget — it goes straight to the author.
faq.subtitleNoWidget: Short answers to what people ask most.
faq.q1: Will it slow down my site?
faq.a1: No. The script is about 15 KB gzipped, loads async and starts when the browser is idle. The screenshot code loads only when it’s needed.
faq.q2: What happens over the Free limit?
faq.a2: Reports are still saved, nothing is lost. We’ll send you a notice, and the extra reports show up in your dashboard as soon as you upgrade to Pro.
faq.q3: Can I use my own button?
faq.a3: Yes. Add data-hide-trigger to the script tag to hide our button, then call Bugping.open() from yours.
faq.q4: Does it work with my site builder?
faq.a4: If you can add a script tag to the page, yes: plain HTML, React, Vue, WordPress, Shopify, Tilda and others. The widget lives in a Shadow DOM, so its styles and yours don’t clash.
faq.a5: The message, its type (bug, idea or question), the visitor’s email if they left one, the screenshot with markup, plus the page URL, browser, OS, screen size, language, time zone and recent console errors.
faq.a6: Password fields are masked in screenshots, tokens in page URLs are redacted and IP addresses are never stored. Screenshots are deleted automatically after 30 days on Free and after a year on Pro.
faq.q7: Can I cancel or get a refund?
faq.a7: Yes. Cancel any time — Pro stays active until the end of the paid period. Within 14 days of the first payment you can get a full refund. Payments and refunds are handled by Paddle.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what data Bugping collects, why, where it is stored and what rights you have. It covers two groups of people: owners who create a Bugping account, and visitors who send feedback through the widget on an owner’s website.

roles.title: Who is responsible for the data
roles.p1: For the account data of owners, Bugping is the controller.
roles.p2: For feedback that visitors send through the widget, the owner of the website is the controller. Bugping processes it on the owner’s behalf and only to store it and deliver it to them. Owners must tell their visitors about the widget in their own privacy policy (see our Terms of Service).

owners.title: Data about account owners
owners.li1: Your email address and, if you sign in with GitHub, your GitHub account id and public profile name.
owners.li2: Your projects and their settings, and the Telegram or Discord destinations you connect. Bot tokens and webhook addresses are stored encrypted.
owners.li3: Your billing status: plan and subscription dates. Payment details are handled by Paddle; we never see or store card numbers.

visitors.title: Data in feedback from website visitors
visitors.p1: What a visitor sends through the widget: the message, an optional email address and an optional screenshot. Before sending, the visitor can review the screenshot, mark it up, hide parts of it or remove it.
visitors.p2: Technical context attached to each report: page address (tokens in query strings are removed), referrer, browser, operating system, screen and window size, language, time zone and recent console errors from that page.
visitors.p3: IP addresses are never stored. A salted hash of the IP address is used only inside short-lived rate-limit keys that stop spam.

purposes.title: Why we use it
purposes.p1: To provide the service: show reports in the dashboard, deliver them to the channels the owner chose, send sign-in links, apply plan limits and process payments. We do not sell data, show ads or use analytics trackers.
purposes.p2: Legal bases under the GDPR: the contract with account owners; the owner’s legitimate interest in receiving feedback about their website, for visitor reports; legal obligations, for billing records.

processors.title: Service providers
processors.li1: Supabase — database, sign-in (including sign-in emails) and file storage, in London, United Kingdom;
processors.li2: Vercel — hosting of the website and its API, in London, United Kingdom;
processors.li3: GitHub — sign-in, if you choose it;
processors.li4: Telegram and Discord — delivery of reports to the chats and channels the owner connects;
processors.li5: Paddle.com — payments and invoicing, as our Merchant of Record.

location.title: Where data is stored
location.p1: Bugping stores data in London, United Kingdom, which the European Commission recognises as providing adequate data protection. Telegram, Discord, GitHub and Paddle process data under their own policies.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.li1: Screenshots: 30 days on the Free plan and 1 year on Pro, then deleted automatically.
retention.li2: Messages, visitor emails and technical context: until the owner deletes the report, the project or the account.
retention.li3: Account data: until you delete your account. Deleting a project or an account removes all related data.
retention.li5: Billing records: as long as tax law requires. Paddle keeps its own records as the seller.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.p1: This website uses only what it needs to work:
cookies.li1: sign-in cookies (Supabase) keep you signed in;
cookies.li2: locale remembers the language you picked;
cookies.li3: tz remembers your time zone so that dates in the dashboard show in your local time;
cookies.li4: bp_next remembers, for 10 minutes, the dashboard page to open after you sign in;
cookies.li5: ref remembers, for 30 days, which Bugping widget sent you here, if you followed a “Powered by Bugping” link;
cookies.li6: theme (in local storage) remembers light or dark mode.
cookies.p2: There are no advertising or analytics cookies. The widget on customers’ websites sets no cookies at all.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.p1: You can ask to access, correct, delete or export your data, to restrict or object to its processing, and to withdraw consent. Account owners can delete projects and their whole account in the dashboard themselves.
rights.p2: If you sent feedback through a website’s widget, contact the owner of that website first; we will help them handle your request. You can always write to us at {email}. We answer within 30 days.
rights.p3: You may also complain to a data protection authority, such as the one in your EU country or, in Ukraine, the Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights.

children.title: Children
children.p1: Bugping is not meant for children under 16, and we do not knowingly collect their data.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.p1: We publish changes on this page and update the date above. If a change significantly affects how we use your data, we will tell account owners before it takes effect.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms apply to your use of Bugping, the feedback and bug-report widget and dashboard on this website. By creating an account you accept them.

service.title: The service
service.p1: Bugping lets you add a widget to your website so that visitors can send feedback with screenshots. Reports appear in your dashboard and can be delivered to Telegram or Discord.

account.title: Your account
account.li1: You must be at least 16 years old and able to enter into a contract.
account.li2: Keep your sign-in email and connected accounts secure. You are responsible for what happens in your account.

use.title: Acceptable use
use.li1: collect data you are not allowed to collect, or sensitive data such as passwords and payment details;
use.li2: send spam, malware or unlawful content, including through Telegram or Discord;
use.li3: attack, overload or reverse-engineer the service, or get around plan limits.

visitors.title: Your visitors’ data
visitors.p1: You are the controller of the feedback your visitors send. You must tell them about the widget in your own privacy policy and have a lawful basis to collect their feedback. We process it only on your behalf, as described in our Privacy Policy.

plans.title: Plans and payments
plans.p1: The Free plan includes one project and 20 reports per month; we may change Free limits with notice. Pro is billed monthly until you cancel it. Lifetime is a one-time payment that keeps Pro features for as long as Bugping operates.
plans.p2: Our order process is conducted by our online reseller Paddle.com. Paddle.com is the Merchant of Record for all our orders. Paddle provides all customer service inquiries and handles returns.
plans.p3: Prices are shown in the Pricing section. Paddle calculates and collects taxes at checkout.

cancel.title: Cancellation
cancel.p1: You can cancel a subscription at any time in Billing. Pro stays active until the end of the paid period. Refunds follow our Refund Policy.

availability.title: Availability and changes
availability.p1: We work to keep Bugping running, but provide it “as is”, without a guarantee of uninterrupted availability. We may change or remove features. If we shut the service down, we will give account owners at least 30 days’ notice.

liability.title: Liability
liability.p1: To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect losses, lost profits or lost data, and our total liability is limited to what you paid us in the 12 months before the claim.

termination.title: Suspension and termination
termination.p1: We may suspend or close accounts that break these terms or abuse the service or its delivery channels. You can delete your account at any time in the dashboard.

law.title: Governing law
law.p1: These terms are governed by the law of Ukraine. This does not take away the protection that consumer law in your country gives you.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.p1: We may update these terms; the date above shows the current version. If a change is significant, we will tell account owners before it takes effect.

refund.title: Refund Policy
refund.intro: We want you to pay only for Bugping if it works for you.

window.title: Full refund within 14 days
window.p1: You can get a full refund within 14 days of the first payment of a subscription or of a Lifetime purchase, no questions asked.

after.title: After 14 days
after.p1: A monthly subscription can be cancelled at any time and stays active until the end of the paid period. The current period is not refunded.

how.title: How to ask for a refund
how.p1: Reply to your Paddle receipt email, or write to us at {email} from the address you paid with. Refunds are processed by Paddle, our Merchant of Record, to the original payment method.

effect.title: After a refund
effect.p1: Your account returns to the Free plan. Your projects and reports stay, and Free limits apply again.

installGuide.title: Install Bugping on your site
installGuide.metaDescription: How to add the Bugping feedback widget to any website, WordPress, Shopify, Tilda or Next.js.
installGuide.intro: Bugping works on any site where you can add a script tag. Pick your platform and follow the steps — it takes about two minutes.
installGuide.keyNote: This example uses a placeholder key. After you sign up, the Install page shows the snippet with your project's real key.
installGuide.allowedHint: If you limited reports to your website in Settings, also add the address you actually use — for example your-store.myshopify.com or project123.tilda.ws — or leave the list empty to accept reports from any site.

html.title: Any website (HTML)
html.step1: Open the HTML template that every page of your site uses.
html.step2: Paste the code right before the closing '</body>' tag.
html.step3: Publish the change and open your site: the widget button appears in the corner.

wordpress.title: WordPress
wordpress.step1: In your WordPress admin, open Plugins → Add New, search for “WPCode” and install and activate “WPCode – Insert Headers and Footers”.
wordpress.step3: Paste the code into the Footer box and click Save Changes.
wordpress.note: Prefer a plugin to editing theme files: theme updates overwrite them, and block themes have no header.php.

shopify.title: Shopify
shopify.step1: In your Shopify admin, open Online Store → Themes.
shopify.step2: Next to your current theme, open the … menu and choose Edit code.
shopify.step3: Open layout/theme.liquid, paste the code right before '</body>' and click Save.
shopify.note: Shopify doesn’t allow custom scripts on checkout pages, so the widget shows on your store pages but not in checkout.

tilda.title: Tilda
tilda.step2: Find the HTML code for the HEAD section, click Edit, paste the code and save.
tilda.step3: Click Publish all pages so every page gets the widget.
tilda.note: Adding your own code on Tilda may require a paid plan. Menu names can differ slightly between Tilda versions.

nextjs.title: Next.js
nextjs.step1: Add the Script component to your root layout (app/layout.tsx or pages/_app.tsx).
nextjs.step2: Deploy: the widget loads after the page becomes interactive.
